mock_data.title: Advances in Detection
mock_data.passage:
A man received a life sentence for murder in London recently. What is unusual about this is that the murder took place 18 years ago. At the time the murder was committed, the man, Anthony Ruark, was questioned by the police, but their investigations did not reveal enough evidence for them to charge him. He claimed to have an alibi for the time of the crime.

Ruark clearly thought that he had got away with the murder. The murdered woman, who was strangled, had been his girlfriend at one time and he continued to be friendly with her family after her death. He showed no signs that there was a murder on his conscience for all these years.

His conviction was partly due to modern advances in crime detection and partly to chance. Genetic fingerprinting, based on DNA patterns, is now an important part of forensic science, but it was not developed in the UK until after the murder. The process depends on obtaining a sample of the suspect's blood, saliva, skin, or other material that contains body cells, and so DNA. It has been discovered that the number and pattern of certain repeated sequences in human DNA appear to be unique to each individual, making it a valuable and accurate means of identification.

Computers also played a part in Ruark's eventual conviction. When he was convicted of a crime last year, details of his DNA were automatically included on a police database. At the time the police were already re-investigating the 1983 murder, and Ruark's possible part in it, following a telephone tip-off from a member of the public.

A forensic sample taken from the murder scene was analysed, using DNA profiling, and the analysis revealed that the DNA matched Ruark's. He had left some body samples at the scene of the crime and this is what led to his conviction so many years later.

This has been seen as a great victory for modern forensic techniques. It was the murderer's own body that proved him guilty.
mock_data.passageB1:
A man in London has been sentenced to prison for life for murder. This is surprising because the murder happened 18 years ago. At that time, the police questioned the man, Anthony Ruark. But they did not find enough evidence to charge him with the crime. He said he was somewhere else when the murder happened.

Ruark probably thought he would not be caught. The woman who was murdered, who was strangled, used to be his girlfriend. He was still friends with her family after she died. He seemed like he had no guilt about the murder for many years.

His conviction was partly because of new ways to detect crime and partly because of luck. Now, genetic fingerprinting, which uses DNA, is important in crime investigations. But it was not used in the UK when the murder happened. This process needs a sample of blood, saliva, skin, or something else from the person. This contains DNA. Scientists found that everyone has a different pattern in their DNA. This makes it a very good way to identify people.

Computers also helped to convict Ruark. When he was found guilty of another crime last year, his DNA was put on a police database. At that time, the police were already looking again at the 1983 murder. They were investigating Ruark because someone had tipped off the police by phone.

A sample from the murder scene was analysed using DNA. The analysis showed that the DNA was the same as Ruark's. He had left some body samples at the place where the crime happened. This is why he was found guilty after so many years.

This is seen as a big success for modern crime-solving methods. The murderer's own body proved he was guilty.
mock_data.passageB2:
A man in London has recently been sentenced to life imprisonment for a murder committed 18 years ago. What makes this case so remarkable is that Anthony Ruark, the convicted man, was initially questioned by the police shortly after the crime. However, at the time, the police investigation didn't uncover enough evidence to formally charge him. He even had an alibi, claiming he was elsewhere when the murder took place.

Ruark must have believed he had successfully evaded justice. The victim, who had been strangled, was a former girlfriend. He even maintained friendly relationships with her family after her death, showing no outward signs of guilt or a troubled conscience throughout the years.

His eventual conviction was a result of both advancements in forensic science and a degree of luck. DNA fingerprinting, which relies on unique DNA patterns, is now a crucial tool in forensic investigations. However, this technology wasn't available in the UK until after the murder. The process involves obtaining a sample of the suspect's blood, saliva, skin, or other bodily material containing cells and therefore DNA. Scientists discovered that the number and arrangement of certain repeated DNA sequences are unique to each individual, making it a highly accurate identification method.

Computers also played a significant role in Ruark's subsequent conviction. After being convicted of a separate crime last year, his DNA profile was automatically added to a national police database. Around the same time, the police had already begun re-examining the 1983 murder, specifically Ruark's possible involvement, due to a telephone tip-off from a member of the public. This information prompted them to delve deeper into the cold case.

A forensic sample taken from the original crime scene was then analysed using DNA profiling. The results showed a clear match between the DNA found at the scene and Ruark's DNA profile. He had unknowingly left biological samples at the crime scene, and this evidence ultimately led to his conviction so many years later. This case has been hailed as a major success for modern forensic science, demonstrating how a perpetrator's own body can seal their fate.
mock_data.passageC1:
The recent life sentence handed down in London for a murder committed nearly two decades prior underscores the ever-increasing reach of forensic science. What renders this case particularly noteworthy is that Anthony Ruark, though initially questioned in the wake of the 1983 crime, evaded prosecution due to a paucity of evidence. He maintained an alibi that, at the time, proved insurmountable for investigators.

Ruark, it would appear, operated under the presumption that he had successfully evaded justice. Despite having once been romantically involved with the victim, who died by strangulation, he maintained cordial relations with her family, seemingly devoid of any discernible remorse for his actions. His conviction, therefore, represents a confluence of both technological advancement and serendipity.

The linchpin of the prosecution's case rested upon advancements in DNA technology. While genetic fingerprinting, a cornerstone of modern forensic analysis, was not yet fully realised in the UK at the time of the murder, its subsequent development proved instrumental. The process, predicated on obtaining biological samples such as blood, saliva, or skin cells, leverages the inherent uniqueness of individual DNA profiles. Specifically, the identification and analysis of variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs) within human DNA have proven to be an exceptionally reliable means of establishing identity, thereby revolutionising crime detection.

Computers, too, played an indispensable role in Ruark's eventual apprehension. His DNA profile, obtained following a conviction for a separate crime the previous year, was automatically uploaded to a national police database. This coincided with the re-opening of the 1983 murder investigation, spurred by an anonymous tip-off, thereby catapulting Ruark back into the frame as a prime suspect. It could be argued that the synergy between technological advancement and human intelligence was key to cracking the case.

Subsequent forensic analysis of samples collected at the original crime scene, utilising advanced DNA profiling techniques, conclusively linked Ruark to the murder. The presence of his biological material at the scene, undetected for nearly two decades, served as the definitive evidence that secured his conviction. This case stands as a testament to the power of modern forensic science, illustrating how the perpetrator's own biology can, ultimately, serve as his undoing and bring closure to decades old cases.

mock_data.translation:
Yaqinda Londonda bir erkak qotillik uchun umrbod qamoq jazosiga hukm qilindi. Buning g'ayrioddiyligi shundaki, qotillik 18 yil oldin sodir bo'lgan. Qotillik sodir etilgan vaqtda Entoni Ruark nomli erkak politsiya tomonidan so'roq qilingan, ammo ularning tergovlari uni ayblov qo'yish uchun etarli dalillarni aniqlashga olmagan. U jinoyat sodir bo'lgan vaqtda alibi borligini da'vo qilgan.

Ruark qotillikdan qutulib qolganga ishongan. Bo'g'ilib o'ldirilgan ayol bir vaqtlar uning qiz do'sti bo'lgan va u o'limidan keyin ham uning oilasi bilan do'stona munosabatda bo'lishda davom etgan. U shu yillar davomida qotillik vijdonida turganining hech qanday belgilarini ko'rsatmadi.

Uning ayblanishi qisman jinoyatni aniqlashdagi zamonaviy yutuqlar va qisman tasodifga bog'liq edi. DNK naqshlariga asoslangan genetik barmoq izi hozirda sud-tibbiy fanning muhim qismi hisoblanadi, ammo u Buyuk Britaniyada qotillikdan keyin ishlab chiqilgan. Jarayon gumonlanuvchining qoni, tupugi, terisi yoki tana hujayralarini va shuning uchun DNKni o'z ichiga olgan boshqa materialdan namuna olishga bog'liq. Inson DNKsidagi ma'lum takrorlanuvchi ketma-ketliklarning soni va naqshi har bir shaxsga xos ekanligi aniqlandi, bu esa uni qimmatli va aniq identifikatsiya vositasiga aylantiradi.

Kompyuterlar ham Ruarkning oxir-oqibatdagi ayblanishida rol o'ynadi. O'tgan yili u jinoyat uchun hukm qilinganda, uning DNK tafsilotlari avtomatik ravishda politsiya ma'lumotlar bazasiga kiritilgan. O'sha paytda politsiya allaqachon 1983 yildagi qotillikni va Ruarkning undagi mumkin bo'lgan rolini jamoatchilik a'zosidan telefon orqali olingan ma'lumotdan keyin qayta tekshirayotgan edi.

Qotillik joyidan olingan sud-tibbiy namuna DNK profillashtirish yordamida tahlil qilindi va tahlil DNKning Ruarkniki bilan mos kelishini aniqladi. U jinoyat joyida ba'zi tana namunalarini qoldirgan va bu uning ko'p yillar o'tib ayblanishiga sabab bo'lgan.

Bu zamonaviy sud-tibbiy texnikaning buyuk g'alabasi sifatida ko'rildi. Qotilning aybdorligini o'z tanasi isbotladi.

mock_data.translationB2:
Londonda bir erkak 18 yil oldin sodir etilgan qotillik uchun umrbod qamoq jazosiga hukm qilindi. Bu ishni shunchalik e'tiborga molik qiladigan narsa shundaki, ayblanuvchi Entoni Ruark dastlab jinoyatdan ko'p o'tmay politsiya tomonidan so'roq qilingan. Ammo, o'sha paytda politsiya tergovi uni rasman ayblash uchun yetarli dalillarni aniqlay olmadi. U hatto qotillik sodir bo'lgan paytda boshqa joyda bo'lganini da'vo qilib, oqlanishga ham ega edi.

Ruark adolatdan muvaffaqiyatli qutulib qoldim deb o'ylagan bo'lsa kerak. Bo'g'ib o'ldirilgan qurbon uning sobiq qiz do'sti edi. U hatto o'limidan keyin ham uning oilasi bilan do'stona munosabatlarni saqlab qoldi va yillar davomida hech qanday tashqi aybdorlik yoki vijdon azobi alomatlarini ko'rsatmadi.

Uning oxir-oqibat hukm qilinishi ham sud tibbiyoti sohasidagi yutuqlar, ham omad natijasi bo'ldi. DNK barmoq izlari, noyob DNK namunalariga asoslangan holda, hozirda sud-tibbiy tekshiruvlarda muhim vosita hisoblanadi. Ammo, bu texnologiya Buyuk Britaniyada qotillikdan keyingina paydo bo'ldi. Jarayon gumonlanuvchining qoni, so'lagi, terisi yoki hujayralarni va shuning uchun DNKni o'z ichiga olgan boshqa tana materialidan namunani olishni o'z ichiga oladi. Olimlar ma'lum takroriy DNK ketma-ketliklarining soni va joylashuvi har bir shaxs uchun noyob ekanligini aniqladilar, bu uni juda aniq identifikatsiya usuliga aylantiradi.

Kompyuterlar ham Ruarkning keyingi hukm qilinishida muhim rol o'ynadi. O'tgan yili alohida jinoyatda aybdor deb topilgandan so'ng, uning DNK profili avtomatik ravishda milliy politsiya ma'lumotlar bazasiga qo'shildi. Ayni paytda, politsiya allaqachon 1983 yildagi qotillikni, xususan, Ruarkning mumkin bo'lgan ishtirokini, jamoatchilikdan olingan telefon xabari tufayli qayta ko'rib chiqa boshlagan edi. Bu ma'lumot ularni bu eski ishni chuqurroq o'rganishga undadi.

Keyin asl jinoyat joyidan olingan sud-tibbiy namunasi DNK profilidan foydalanib tahlil qilindi. Natijalar jinoyat joyida topilgan DNK va Ruarkning DNK profili o'rtasida aniq moslikni ko'rsatdi. U bilmagan holda jinoyat joyida biologik namunalarni qoldirgan edi va bu dalil oxir-oqibat ko'p yillar o'tib uning hukmiga olib keldi. Bu ish zamonaviy sud tibbiyotining asosiy muvaffaqiyati sifatida e'tirof etildi va jinoyatchining o'z tanasi qanday qilib ularning taqdirini hal qilishi mumkinligini ko'rsatdi.
mock_data.translationC1:
Yaqinda Londonda qariyb yigirma yil avval sodir etilgan qotillik uchun umrbod qamoq jazosining berilishi sud-tibbiyot fanining tobora kengayib borayotgan ta'sirini ko'rsatadi. Bu ishni ayniqsa e'tiborga molik qiladigan narsa shundaki, Entoni Ruark, 1983-yildagi jinoyatdan so'ng dastlab so'roq qilingan bo'lsa-da, dalillarning yetishmasligi tufayli jinoiy javobgarlikka tortilmadi. U o'sha paytda tergovchilar uchun yengib bo'lmas bo'lgan alibini saqlab qoldi.

Ko'rinishidan, Ruark adolatdan muvaffaqiyatli qochib qutuldim, degan taxmin ostida harakat qilgan. Bir vaqtlar bo'g'ib o'ldirilgan jabrlanuvchi bilan romantik munosabatda bo'lganiga qaramay, u uning oilasi bilan samimiy munosabatlarni saqlab qoldi, go'yo o'z harakatlaridan hech qanday sezilarli pushaymonlik sezilmagandek. Shuning uchun uning hukmi texnologik taraqqiyot va omadning birgalikdagi natijasidir.

Prokuratura ishining asosiy tayanchi DNK texnologiyasidagi yutuqlarga asoslangan edi. Zamonaviy sud-tibbiy tahlilning asosi bo'lgan genetik barmoq izlari, qotillik sodir bo'lgan paytda Buyuk Britaniyada to'liq amalga oshirilmagan bo'lsa-da, uning keyingi rivojlanishi muhim rol o'ynadi. Qon, so'lak yoki teri hujayralari kabi biologik namunalarni olishga asoslangan jarayon individual DNK profillarining o'ziga xosligidan foydalanadi. Xususan, inson DNKsida o'zgaruvchan sonli tandem takrorlanishlarini (VNTR) aniqlash va tahlil qilish shaxsni aniqlashning juda ishonchli usuli ekanligi isbotlandi va shu bilan jinoyatni aniqlashda inqilob qildi.

Kompyuterlar ham Ruarkni oxir-oqibat ushlashda ajralmas rol o'ynadi. Uning o'tgan yili alohida jinoyat uchun hukm qilinganidan so'ng olingan DNK profili avtomatik ravishda milliy politsiya ma'lumotlar bazasiga yuklandi. Bu 1983-yildagi qotillik tergovining qayta ochilishi bilan bir vaqtga to'g'ri keldi, bu esa anonim xabar bilan turtki bo'ldi va shu bilan Ruarkni asosiy gumonlanuvchi sifatida qayta olib chiqdi. Texnologik taraqqiyot va inson aql-zakovati o'rtasidagi sinergiya ishni hal qilishning kaliti bo'ldi, deb ta'kidlash mumkin.

Dastlabki jinoyat joyida to'plangan namunalarni keyingi sud-tibbiy tahlili, ilg'or DNK profillash usullaridan foydalangan holda, Ruarkning qotillikka aloqadorligini yakuniy tarzda isbotladi. Uning biologik materialining deyarli yigirma yil davomida aniqlanmagan holda voqea joyida bo'lishi uning hukmini ta'minlagan qat'iy dalil bo'lib xizmat qildi. Ushbu ish zamonaviy sud-tibbiyot fanining kuchidan dalolat beradi, bu jinoyatchining o'z biologiyasi qanday qilib oxir-oqibatda uning halokatiga olib kelishi va o'nlab yillar davom etgan ishlarga nuqta qo'yishini ko'rsatadi.
